video_title: Question For The Fed: Where Is Waldo?
gist: Ed Yardeni's weekend market call (recorded Oct 18) argues the AI-trade selloff, driven by bond vigilantes targeting indebted AI borrowers, is a pullback within a bull market, keeps S&P forward EPS at 425 and a 7,900 target with caution on valuation, and downgrades Go Global to market weight. The Fed 'Where's Waldo' briefing gets only a brief mention near the end (two more hikes to neutral).

themes.theme: AI trade unwind and bond vigilantes

insights.claim: Yardeni says the AI trade 'went bonkers' over the prior two weeks, with some AI stocks in a bear market, as Gartner-style research questions whether hyperscaler and neo-cloud capex can be matched by realistic revenue projections.
insights.speaker: Ed Yardeni
insights.so_what: Capex-versus-revenue doubts are the trigger for the AI drawdown.
insights.quote: The AI trade has totally gone bonkers last week and maybe the week before that.

insights.claim: Bond vigilantes have shifted focus from sovereign debt to AI-related bonds, punishing highly indebted AI names such as CoreWeave with higher yields.
insights.speaker: Ed Yardeni
insights.so_what: Credit-market pricing is now a constraint on leveraged AI buildout.
insights.quote: all of a sudden in the bond vigilantes have been focusing on AI bonds.

insights.claim: Yardeni views higher funding costs for indebted, unproven AI companies as healthy because markets, not rating agencies, should price credit and curb excesses in the AI trade.
insights.speaker: Ed Yardeni
insights.so_what: Expect weaker, leveraged AI names to be filtered out while the technology persists.

insights.claim: The AI correction triggered safe-haven buying of Treasuries, easing worries that rising yields would cause a credit crunch and recession; the two-year stopped rising and the yield curve flattened.
insights.speaker: Ed Yardeni
insights.so_what: AI equity weakness is acting as a hedge against the bond-yield threat to the economy.

insights.claim: AI is 'the real deal' and a probably revolutionary, sustainable technology, especially combined with humanoid robotics and automation, but the open question is how to invest in it and whether data center and chip spending earns a decent return.
insights.speaker: Ed Yardeni
insights.so_what: Technology durability is separated from investment returns on capex.
insights.quote: AI itself is not going to fail. AI is the real deal.

insights.claim: Cheaper Chinese open-source models create a competitive marketplace, and Yardeni argues margins will not stay as high as in parts of the AI trade, particularly semiconductors.
insights.speaker: Ed Yardeni
insights.so_what: Margin compression is a risk for AI hardware and model leaders.
insights.quote: competitive marketplaces margins don't stay as high as we're seeing in some of these areas of the AI trade, particularly semiconductors.

insights.claim: Semiconductors still trade as cyclicals, with PEs lowest when earnings peak, and there is an open debate whether they have become secular; Yardeni says nobody knows and expects profit-taking after big gains.
insights.speaker: Ed Yardeni
insights.so_what: Low PEs on peak earnings are a cyclical warning, not a bargain signal, if cyclicality persists.

insights.claim: Because winners and losers in AI are too hard to pick, Yardeni recommends buying the Nasdaq 100 and holding it, expecting winners to keep winning and losers to drop out; he sees interesting buying opportunities in tech on the pullback.
insights.speaker: Ed Yardeni
insights.so_what: A diversified index approach to AI exposure at lower prices.

insights.claim: The 10-year Treasury yield is slightly above 5%, and Yardeni now finds it very attractive after the AI-driven reprieve.
insights.speaker: Ed Yardeni
insights.so_what: Yardeni sees value in duration at 5%-plus yields.

insights.claim: Almost all of the 2026 rise in the nominal 10-year Treasury yield is attributable to the TIPS yield, now about 2.9%, which tracks the NY Fed weekly economic indicator (a real GDP growth proxy) closely over three years.
insights.speaker: Ed Yardeni
insights.so_what: Yardeni reads high yields as strong growth rather than fiscal or inflation stress; the WEI is a real-time gauge to watch.

insights.claim: The market-based inflation proxy (nominal minus TIPS) has stayed around 2.5% to 3% even after hotter CPI and PPI, suggesting investors holding 10-year bonds remain calm about inflation.
insights.speaker: Ed Yardeni
insights.so_what: Breakevens show no de-anchoring of inflation expectations despite hot prints.

insights.claim: The trailing 12-month federal deficit through September is $1.99 trillion; Yardeni calls $2 trillion deficits in a growing economy unsustainable, but says the question is when it causes trouble.
insights.speaker: Ed Yardeni
insights.so_what: Fiscal risk is acknowledged but not seen as the current driver of yields.

insights.claim: Yardeni says two more Fed rate hikes should bring policy back to neutral, and then 'ask us again', implying the Fed may be near the end of its cycle.
insights.speaker: Ed Yardeni
insights.so_what: A hiking path to neutral is the stated Fed base case in the accompanying morning briefing.
insights.quote: We think two more rate hikes should get us back to neutral and then ask us again.

insights.claim: The Strait of Hormuz situation never de-escalated; Iranians are attacking cargo ships and one ship hit a mine and sank, and Trump has said he will address Iran after the midterms, leaving risk of an October surprise from either side.
insights.speaker: Ed Yardeni
insights.so_what: Oil-price and re-escalation risk sits ahead of the midterms.

insights.claim: Yardeni stays bullish on gold, which rose to about 5,500 on central bank buying (Russia, China, Iran) before falling on the war, forced selling by central banks like Turkey's amid higher oil prices, and higher global bond yields.
insights.speaker: Ed Yardeni
insights.so_what: Gold may resume rising once bond yields stabilize and central bank buying returns.
insights.quote: I'm not giving up on gold yet.

insights.claim: Since September 15 Yardeni Research has advised proceeding with caution, defined as anything from a garden-variety pullback to a correction or bear market; it moved its 8,400 S&P 500 target out to mid-next year and uses 7,900 now.
insights.speaker: Ed Yardeni
insights.so_what: The firm cut the near-term index target for valuation, not earnings, reasons.

insights.claim: The earnings outlook is unchanged; the caution is about valuation, with forward earnings converging on the firm's 425 forecast (about 424.19 at last reading) after lowering forward PE assumptions.
insights.speaker: Ed Yardeni
insights.so_what: Earnings are the support; multiple compression is the risk.

insights.claim: The 2028 S&P 500 earnings estimate has risen to $492.62, which Yardeni calls potentially irrational exuberance, while he forecasts $500 for 2030 and, at 20 times discounted at end-2029, an S&P 500 of 10,000 by the end of the decade.
insights.speaker: Ed Yardeni
insights.so_what: Analyst estimates are seen as too high near term, yet the decade-end 10,000 target is intact.
insights.quote: I just uh think this number is way too high

insights.claim: Q3 S&P 500 earnings growth is tracking about 24% and Q4 about 29.8%; the roughly 50% growth figure in an earlier quarter was inflated by mark-to-market gains at Alphabet and Amazon, and is nearer 25% excluding them.
insights.speaker: Ed Yardeni
insights.so_what: Underlying growth is strong but earlier prints overstated by investment marks.

insights.claim: Earnings have been fabulous while PEs have fallen (FEMO offset by FOMO), in both the US and globally, so investors are not chasing multiples higher.
insights.speaker: Ed Yardeni
insights.so_what: Falling multiples on rising earnings point to cheaper valuations.

insights.claim: Yardeni is firmly in the no-recession camp and expects analysts' optimistic estimates to prove right as long as there is no recession.
insights.speaker: Ed Yardeni
insights.so_what: The earnings thesis hinges on avoiding recession.

insights.claim: Yardeni Research cut its Go Global recommendation to market weight after the US was getting pricey; it had been in the stay-home camp from 2010 to end-2025 and switched to overweight international late last year.
insights.speaker: Ed Yardeni
insights.so_what: The firm is neutral between US and international equities.

insights.claim: The US is 65% of the MSCI All Country World index, so Yardeni will not recommend overweighting it and prefers market weight.
insights.speaker: Ed Yardeni
insights.so_what: A large US weight limits the case for further US overweights.

insights.claim: French 10-year spreads over Germany are widening dramatically, and Yardeni sees a Greece-2010-style bond vigilante episode brewing in France, where fiscal conservatism sparks riots; he is not excited about Europe.
insights.speaker: Ed Yardeni
insights.so_what: French sovereign debt is a stress point; Greek yields now sit below France and Italy after reforms.

insights.claim: China's exports and imports are soaring, but real retail sales have been flat for about a year because of an aging population and household wealth concentrated in real estate; Yardeni sees China as a possible surprise shock, including a credit system implosion.
insights.speaker: Ed Yardeni
insights.so_what: China's domestic weakness and property exposure are a tail risk for global markets.
